entities.summary:
Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) is an Islamist Palestinian armed movement founded in the early 1980s by militants who broke from Muslim Brotherhood currents toward a more immediate jihad strategy against Israel. Smaller than Hamas, it has remained a persistent actor in Gaza and West Bank militant politics.

PIJ’s ideology fuses Palestinian nationalism with Islamist mobilisation, rejecting negotiated settlement frameworks and aligning at times with Iranian regional support networks. Its attacks and rocket fire have repeatedly shaped ceasefire diplomacy and Israeli military responses.

In the fragmented Palestinian political field, PIJ illustrates how specialised armed organisations can punch above their organisational size by leveraging ideology, external patronage, and cycles of escalation.
